In Colchani, you will learn about salt extraction and processing and see the work of local artisans. On the salt flat, the route includes the Playa Blanca Salt Museum, the saltwater springs of Ojos del Salar, geometric patterns on the salt surface and piles of salt.

The drive across Uyuni's white expanse includes a stop for a picnic lunch. You will then visit Incahuasi Island with its giant cacti, some reaching 12 metres in height. At the end of the day, you will watch the sunset over the salt flat.

The salt flat changes appearance with the seasons. From April to November, geometric patterns are visible on the dry surface; from December to March, water can create mirror-like reflections. Access to Incahuasi and other areas depends on water levels and weather and is confirmed for the selected dates.

In the dry season, the Salar de Uyuni appears as a white salt plain, while in the rainy season its surface becomes an enormous mirror.

On the first day, departure from the hotel is scheduled for 06:30. The route passes Laguna Verde with views of Licancabur Volcano, Dalí Valley, Polques Hot Springs and the Sol de Mañana geysers. You will then see Laguna Colorada at an altitude of around 4,400 metres, where James's flamingos can be found. The overnight stay is at an expedition-style hotel in the desert.

On the second day, the route continues past the small lagoons of Honda, Iar Cacota, Hedionda and Cañapa. Next comes a stop at an Ollagüe Volcano viewpoint and a drive across the Chiguana Salt Flats.

The main highlight of day two is the Salar de Uyuni. According to the source programme, the salt flat lies at around 3,650 metres above sea level, covers approximately 11,000 square kilometres and has a salt layer up to 10 metres thick in its centre. Along the way, you will see Colchani, Ojos de Agua and Fish Island with its giant cacti. A packed lunch is included on this day.

Uyuni lies at an altitude of around 3,800 metres, so symptoms of altitude sickness may occur.

The route across Bolivia's southern Altiplano begins at the Train Cemetery near Uyuni. Old locomotives and railway carriages recall Bolivia's 19th-century railway history.

The road then passes through settlements in Sud Lípez, including the mining town of San Cristóbal. In Stone Valley, you will see red rock formations; dry, high-altitude landscapes open up around Ollagüe Volcano.

Lunch is taken along the way. You will then visit the Joyas Andinas lagoons, the "Andean Jewels," set among volcanoes and desert plains. The precise stops at individual lagoons are confirmed for the selected programme. The journey ends at Ojo de Perdiz; accommodation and onward travel depend on the chosen tour.
